findings.issue: AttentionItem.PartyAr is populated only for correspondence (from PartyNameSnapshot). It is hard-coded to null for commitments, cases and decisions even though commitments.party_id and cases.party_id exist and parties.Name is available (db.Parties is mapped). The B2 spec names «الجهة» as a column of BOTH the W08 «يحتاج إجراءً اليوم» list and the W09 table, so on the screens that column will be permanently blank for every commitment and case row — the reviewer criterion 'directly consumable by the B2 screens (entity references for navigation)' is not met for that field. No test in tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests asserts PartyAr at all, which is why the gap survived.
findings.fix: In AttentionService.ReadAllAsync, project c.PartyId for commitments and cases (and the owning party for decisions if the data model has one). After the six per-table reads, collect the distinct non-null party ids and issue ONE extra query — db.Parties.AsNoTracking().Where(p => ids.Contains(p.Id)).Select(p => new { p.Id, p.Name }) — into a Dictionary<Guid,string>, then fill PartyAr from it when building the AttentionItem rows (leave null when the party row is gone). One added query keeps the measured 48 ms well inside the 200 ms budget. Add a test asserting a commitment and a case whose party_id points at a named party surface that name in PartyAr, and that a row with no party still yields null.

findings.issue: notifications has only ix_notifications_due_at (src/Wakeel.Core/Migrations, line 143) — no index on source or created_at. RunOnceAsync loads EVERY notification source written in the last 400 days into a HashSet on every minute tick (a full table scan plus a full materialization), NotificationService.CreateAsync scans the table once per key, and GetPanelAsync sorts the whole table by created_at. Nothing ever prunes notifications (dismissed rows are deliberately kept for key retention), so the per-minute cost grows for the life of the installation.
findings.fix: Add ix_notifications_source and ix_notifications_created_at in a NEW migration file under src/Wakeel.Core/Migrations (never edit a shipped one), and narrow the pre-load to reminder keys only: .Where(n => n.Source != null && n.Source.StartsWith(ReminderScheduler.KeyPrefix) && n.CreatedAt >= keyFloor). Optionally add a retention sweep of dismissed notifications older than KeyRetention so the table stops growing without bound.

findings.issue: The ten-minute timer callback calls CheckAsync with the default CancellationToken and ClockGuard holds no CancellationTokenSource, unlike TimeProviderMinuteTicker which cancels its in-flight tick in StopCore(). Stop()/Dispose() therefore disposes the timer but lets a pass that is already inside dispatcher(...) keep reading and writing a database session that the sign-out is tearing down.
findings.fix: Give ClockGuard the same shape as TimeProviderMinuteTicker: create a CancellationTokenSource in StartAsync (inside the lock, after cancelling and disposing the previous one), pass its token into CheckAsync from the timer callback, catch OperationCanceledException separately, and cancel + dispose it in Stop().

findings.issue: CheckSyncAsync projects d.EmployeeName but never uses it (the message is built from the device KIND label only). Dead projection today, and a latent privacy problem: the exported health report is a file the user shares with support, and an employee's name does not belong in it.
findings.fix: Drop EmployeeName from the Select in CheckSyncAsync — project only { d.Kind, d.LastSyncAt }.

findings.issue: Two card statuses diverge from the W12 mockup (design/exports/preview/*/W/W12): the mockup renders a missing/unreachable scanner as «عطل» with «إعادة الاكتشاف», and «آخر مزامنة» as «تحذير» when the last sync is stale. CheckScannerAsync always returns Warning, and CheckSyncAsync returns Ok whenever ANY non-revoked device has ever synced, however long ago — so a device that last synced weeks back still shows «سليم».
findings.fix: Decide the scanner severity with the owner and record it in the file's remarks either way. For sync, add a staleness threshold constant (e.g. SyncWarningDays, mirroring BackupWarningDays) and return Warning with HealthActions.OpenSync when the newest LastSyncAt across kinds is older than it; add a test seeding a device synced 10 days ago and asserting Warning.

findings.issue: The package's user-facing Arabic lives in src/Wakeel.Core/Services/CoreAr.cs, not in src/Wakeel.Design/Text/Ar.*.cs as the standing rule requires. The file documents the reason (Core is referenced BY Design/UI, so it cannot reference Design without inverting the layering) and Core genuinely must emit finished Arabic (notification rows are persisted, health cards carry «رسالة عربية»). It is a reasoned deviation, not an oversight, but it is still a deviation the owner has not ratified.
findings.fix: No code change without a ruling. Raise it explicitly with the owner: either ratify CoreAr.cs as the Core-layer equivalent of Ar.*.cs (and say so in ARCHITECTURE.md §12), or move the sentences to Wakeel.Design/Text/Ar.Core.cs and have the UI layer resolve them from the stable English ids Core already exposes (HealthComponents/HealthActions/NotificationKinds).

findings.issue: PersistAsync calls ExecuteDeleteAsync (which executes immediately, outside the change tracker) BEFORE SaveChangesAsync, with no enclosing transaction. If the save then fails, the 90-day prune is already committed while the new snapshots are not — the history loses rows without gaining the ones that justified the prune.
findings.fix: Wrap the two operations the way QuickCaptureService.CaptureExpenseAsync already does: begin a transaction when db.Database.CurrentTransaction is null, SaveChangesAsync first, then ExecuteDeleteAsync, then commit; dispose in a finally and respect a caller-owned transaction.

findings.issue: After round 2 moved the attention window onto the user's local day, two day counts were left on UTC: ReadBackupStateAsync computes days as (utcNow.Date - last.Date).TotalDays, and ReminderScheduler's backupAgeDays does the same. In a UTC+3 office, between local midnight and 03:00 those counts are one day behind the local day the KPI cards use, so «مضى 7 أيام» and the backup-overdue flag flip a few hours later than «متأخر» does on the same screen.
findings.fix: Use AttentionWindow.StartOfLocalDay / the window's LocalToday for both: convert last.At and now to the local zone before taking .Date, exactly as AttentionWindow.DaysLate now does. Add a test at 01:00 local asserting the backup age matches the age computed at 09:00 the same local day.

missing_spec_items: «مهمة خلفية كل دقيقة» and «يشغّل ClockCheckService عند التشغيل وكل 10 دقائق» do not actually happen in the running product: nothing in the shipped tree calls IClockGuard.StartAsync(now, dispatcher) or IReminderScheduler.Start(ticker, dispatcher), and nothing calls Stop() on sign-out/lock. The plumbing is complete and correct, but the sibling B2 screens/shell package must wire it (passing ComponentBase.InvokeAsync as the BackgroundPassDispatcher).

«وعند الاستيراد» — ClockCheckTrigger.Import is implemented and tested but has no caller; the sync/import package must call IClockGuard.CheckAsync(ClockCheckTrigger.Import, now, importedDeviceTimestamps).
W09's «الجهة» column cannot be rendered for commitments/cases: AttentionItem.PartyAr is always null for them (see the medium finding). This is the one spec item missing INSIDE this package's scope.
The screens themselves (W08, W09, W10, W11, W12, W91, W92, W94), their bUnit tests and the Walkthrough scenario are the sibling screens package, not this one — correctly absent here.

The four Windows probes (Word registry, WIA scanner, disk, WebView2) have no unit tests: tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests targets net10.0 and cannot reference the net10.0-windows host, and adding a test project would require editing Wakeel.slnx. All four ran for real during the host boot. Accepted as-is.

W12's per-card «آخر فحص 10:24» line and the mockup's second detail line / space progress bar have no field on HealthCard (Component, Title, Status, MessageAr, ActionId). The spec's own definition of a card is exactly status+message+action, so this is a screen-composition note, not a service defect: the timestamp must come from HealthReport.CheckedAt, which applies to the whole run.
notes:
VERIFIED CHAIN (all read in full, exit code 0): `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Core` -> 0 warnings / 0 errors (TreatWarningsAsErrors on); `dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests` -> Passed 323 / Failed 0 / Skipped 0 in 17 s; `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Desktop` -> 0/0.

PERFORMANCE (re-measured myself, not taken from the builder's report): `[b2-services] rows=10000 seed=1543ms attention-snapshot=48ms badges-refresh=48ms attention-counts=43ms budget=200ms` — 4x head-room against the spec's 200 ms. The companion test On10kRows_TheServicesStillAgreeWithWhatWasSeeded proves the fast answer is also the right one (the seeder knows its own late/near/stale/pending counts and the service must reproduce them exactly), so the budget test is not measuring a query that returns nothing.

HOST BOOT (done by me, not trusted from the report): Wakeel.Desktop.exe launched with --remote-debugging-port=9333 --window-size=1366x768 and an empty temp --data-folder. /json/version answered (Edg/153.0.4234.32); /json/list showed /first-run. Captured a CDP JPEG over a hand-rolled websocket and LOOKED at it: W02 renders correctly in dark RTL — «مرحبًا بك في التشغيل الأول», the three-step indicator on step 2, the setup-file drop zone, «كلمة مرور الحزمة» with its reveal eye, «فحص الحزمة», footer «الوكيل v0.21 — 16/09/2026 21:15». No server/port/internet/database wording anywhere on screen. Host log held exactly one INF startup line and no errors; process killed, 0 Wakeel.Desktop.exe remaining.

PREVIEWS VIEWED (once each, small JPEGs): W12 light and W08 dark. W08 confirms Money.Shekels is right — the phone-expense rows render «₪ 42.50» / «₪ 25.00» with the sign leading, matching the implementation exactly. W12 is what produced the scanner/sync severity finding.

SECURITY — clean. (a) No secret reaches a notification: reminder bodies carry only titles, times and locations. (b) The health report contains no key material, no file path and no exception text — the database card shows a size, the vault card a file COUNT and a mismatch count (never a sha256 or a vault path), the runtime card deliberately withholds the browser build number. HealthServiceTests.NoMessageMentionsAServerAPortTheInternetOrTheDatabaseEngine asserts the export against خادم/منفذ/إنترنت/SQL/SQLite/PostgreSQL/port/server with every probe forced to fail, so the worst-case text is covered. The one latent leak is the unused EmployeeName projection (low finding above). (c) Background timers cannot run work on the UI thread's session: both StartAsync and Start REQUIRE a BackgroundPassDispatcher with no default value and ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull, both refusals are tested, and APassAndAScreensQuery_ShareTheSessionSafelyWhenBothGoThroughTheShellsDispatcher drives 20 concurrent passes against 20 UI-style query batches on the same WakeelDb through one gate — and drives the tick directly so the ticker's swallowing catch cannot hide a failure. (d) The clock guard cannot be bypassed silently: NumberingBlocked is derived from the verdict alone, «تجاهل مؤقتًا» only clears Visible, and WhileTheClockIsBad_IssuingAnOfficialNumberIsRefused proves OfficialNumberService refuses independently of the guard.

TEST QUALITY — these are behavioural, not tautological. Spot-checked the ones most likely to be circular: AttentionWindowTests pins a custom UTC+3 zone and asserts LateCutoff == 21:00Z (local midnight, NOT 00:00Z) and that the same row classifies identically at 01:00 and 09:00 local — the pre-fix code returned Near then Late, so these are real regression guards. MinuteTickerTests uses a ManualTimeProvider whose timers fire on demand and asserts Start(a)→Start(b) ticks b and never a, leaves exactly one live timer, and none after Stop. HealthServiceTests distinguishes 'a re-run adds nothing' from 'a scanner going missing adds exactly one row with the new status' from 'an ancient row is pruned'. ClockGuardTests asserts the exact Arabic banner strings and that StateChanged fires once for a change and not for a repeat.

ARCHITECTURE NOTES (no action required). Buckets are mutually exclusive by construction and the group badge is the UNION of its items' record sets keyed by (table, id), so item 26's no-double-counting holds — the 10k test asserts the group badge is strictly less than the sum of its item badges, which is the only assertion that would catch a regression to summing. The AttentionService/BadgeService split is right: one attention pass feeds the whole sidebar instead of six queries per bucket. Scoping is right too — IMinuteTicker moved to AddScoped so a tick dies with the session that started it. Correspondence has no assignee column in the data model, so AttentionItem.AssigneeAr being null for correspondence rows (where the W08 mockup shows a name) is a data-model limit, not a service defect — unlike PartyAr, which has a column to read.

WHY 'fix' AND NOT 'accept': build and tests are green and the package is substantially complete and well-argued, but one medium finding stands (PartyAr always null for commitments and cases, which blanks a column the spec names on two screens). It is a contained change — one extra query plus a lookup — and once it lands with a test I would accept.
